channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: Florida Primary Underscores State’s New Identity as a Republican Juggernaut
item.description: Republicans hold every statewide elected office and have drastically swung voter registration in the state. A newly gerrymandered congressional map has added four Republican-leaning seats.

item.title: NPR: In Portland, this soap box derby combines downhill speed with extreme pageantry
item.description: Soap box derbies send motorless cars down a steep incline. At one event, contestants make their cars look like cartoon characters, subway cars, food, and giant animals (among other outlandish shapes).

item.title: BBC News: Russia warns UK will pay for supplying drones to Ukraine
item.description: Russia accuses the UK of escalating the Ukraine war after British-made drones were used in strikes, but the MoD says it stands against Russian aggression.

item.title: The Guardian: Here is the news from the US: Woke 1.0 is over. But what did progressives do wrong? | Nesrine Malik
item.description: A movement with safety, dignity and equality at its heart may now be blamed for the rightwing backlash. But within it were principles worth carrying forwards Every once in a while, the discourse gods send a tablet down t…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Meta lawsuits: Is social media facing a global legal reckoning?
item.description: Meta battles legal challenges in the US, Europe and beyond over platform design and its impact on younger users.

item.title: Ars Technica: Theban tomb reveals how Egyptian burial trends evolved in time
item.description: Practices shifted from individuals buried in coffins to reusing sites for later mummy interments.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: The Cop Who Took On Flock
item.description: After Noel Pichardo called out his city's embrace of Flock surveillance cameras, he was subjected to five internal affairs investigations in less than two years.

item.title: WIRED Science: What Is El Niño, and What Does It Mean for Weather, Water, and the Global Economy?
item.description: This year’s El Niño is shaping up to be the strongest on record. Here’s what to expect.

item.title: WIRED Business: The Powerful Chinese Model Experts Warned About—and Waited for—Is Here
item.description: Z.ai’s latest AI model release could help companies secure their systems—or find its way into the hands of hackers.

item.title: The New Yorker: Nayib Bukele’s Content Machine Is Reshaping Latin America
item.description: How El Salvador’s authoritarian leader loomed over Colombia’s Presidential race.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Hollywood Is Paying Tribute to Hayden Panettiere
item.description: Viola Davis, Connie Britton, and more of Panettiere’s friends and collaborators are sharing memories of the late actress.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: The Fight Over Spence’s Madison Avenue Expansion
item.description: Neighbors think the private school’s expansion plans for a pair of rowhouses around the corner are “just butt ugly.”
